Translingual alt.
(l en da) ((l en d')), (l en teh) (qualifier: informal or dialectal)
Translingual article
1 (n-g: Used before a noun phrase, including a simple noun)
2 # (non-gloss: The definite grammatical article that shows that the noun phrase that immediately follows it is definitely identifiable...)
3 ## (n-g ...because it has already been mentioned, is to be completely specify specified in the same sentence, or very shortly thereafter.) (from 10th c.)
4 ##: ''I’m reading '''the''' book Mary reviewed.'' (Compare ''I’m reading '''a''' book Mary reviewed.'')
5 ##: ''You live on Main Street, don't you? You know, you should tell the mayor '''the''' street needs cleaning.''
6 ##: '''''The''' men and women watched '''the''' man give '''the''' birdseed to '''the''' bird.''
7 ##: '''''the''' street that runs all the way through my hometown''
8 ##* (quote-web 1=en year=2016 url=https://learningenglish.voanews.com/a/lets-learn-english-lesson-5-where-are-you/3168971.html site=VOA Learning English passage=I sleep in '''the''' bedroom! accessdate=12 December 2018 archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170930001420/https://learningenglish.voanews.com/a/lets-learn-english-lesson-5-where-are-you/3168971.html archivedate=30 September 2017)
9 ## (n-g: ...because it is presumed to be definitely known in context or from shared knowledge.)
10 ### (non-gloss: Used before a noun designating something considered to be unique, or of which there is only one at a time.) (from 10th c.)
11 ###: ''No one knows how many galaxies there are in '''the''' universe.''
12 ###: ''God save '''the''' Queen!''
13 ###* (RQ:King James Version Revelation 1 8 column=2 passage=I am Alpha and Omega, '''the''' beginning and '''the''' ending, saith '''the''' Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, '''the''' Almighty.)
14 ### (non-gloss: Used to indicate a certain example of (a noun) which is usually of most concern or most common or familiar.) (from 12th c.)
15 ###: ''No one in '''the''' whole country had seen it before.''
16 ###: ''I don't think I'll get to it until '''the''' morning.''
17 ###: ''Take me to '''the''' airport/station/hospital/office/park/match/meeting/etcetera.''
18 ### (non-gloss: Used before a body part, a family member, a pet (especially of someone previously mentioned), as an alternative to a possessive pronoun.) (from 12th c.)
19 ###: ''A stone hit him on '''the''' head.'' (= “A stone hit him on his head.”)
20 ###: (q: informal) ''How's '''the''' wife?'' (= "How is your wife?")
21 ### (lb en colloquial) (n-g: Precedes a familiar nickname or other term of address.)
22 ###: (usex en How's '''the''' Sal today? footer="How are you, Sal?")
23 ### (n-g: Used in many idiomatic expressions and proverbs to refer to common objects, roles, or situations connected with something definite, in the manner of an analogy)
24 ###: ''square the circle; feel the pinch; beat around the bush; throw the baby out with the bathwater''
25 # (non-gloss: When stressed, indicates that it describes something which is considered to be best or exclusively worthy of attention.) (from 18th c.)
26 # (non-gloss: Used before a noun phrase beginning with superlative or comparative adjective or an ordinal number,  indicating that the noun refers to a single item.)
27 # (non-gloss: Introducing a singular term to be taken generically: preceding a name of something standing for a whole class.) (from 9th c.)
28 # (n-g: Used with the plural of a surname to indicate the entire family.)
29 (n-g: Used with an adjective)
30 # {{non-gloss|Added to a superlative or an ordinal number to make it into a (glossary: substantive).}} (from 9th c.)
31 # (non-gloss: Used before an adjective, indicating all things (especially persons) described by that adjective.) (from 9th c.)
32 # {{non-gloss|Used before a demonym ending in (m en -ish id=nationality) or (m en -ese) to refer to people of a given country collectively.}}
Translingual adv.
1 {{non-gloss|1=With a comparative or with (m en more) and a verb phrase, establishes a correlation with one or more other such comparatives.}}
2 {{non-gloss|1=With a comparative, and often with (m en for it), indicates a result more like said comparative. This can be negated with (m en none).}}
3 (lb en with a superlative adjective) Beyond all others.
